title: Word from São Paulo: CET
topic: The full price of a loan

messages.text: Motorbike loan, R$8,000 over 24 months: only 1.9% a month!
Plus a R$300 opening fee and R$600 loan insurance
R$8,000 over 24 months at 2.3% a month. Nothing else

steps.title: CET · Custo Efetivo Total
steps.body: The "total effective cost". Brazilian lenders have to show it: one rate with interest, fees and insurance all included. It's the [[total-cost-of-credit]], and it's the number to compare, not the headline rate.

steps.prompt: Offer A adds R$900 of fee and insurance to the loan, but Rafa still only gets R$8,000. What does offer A really cost per month?
steps.reveal: About 2.9% a month. Rafa pays back R$8,900 plus interest for R$8,000 in his hand. The "cheap" 1.9% is more expensive than offer B's 2.3%. Simplified: fees are added to the loan.

steps.prompt: Match each part of a loan offer with what it is.
pairs: The price of the borrowed money, per month or year
A one-off charge to set up the loan
An extra paid in case you can't repay
All of it together, as one rate

steps.prompt: Offer A: 1.9% a month, CET 2.9%. Offer B: 2.3% a month, CET 2.3%. Which costs Rafa less?
steps.explanation: Compare the CET, not the headline. B's 2.3% is all there is. A's fees and insurance push it to 2.9%.

steps.prompt: Why might a lender advertise a low rate and add fees on top?
options: The low rate catches the eye, while the fees raise the real cost
Fees make the loan safer for the borrower
steps.explanation: People compare the number they see first. Fees and add-ons are where [[hidden-interest]] lives.

t1.body: It means "total real cost". In Brazil, lenders must show it. It is one number with interest, fees and insurance together. In English: [[total-cost-of-credit]]. Compare this number, not the first one you see.

p1.prompt: Offer A adds R$900 for the fee and insurance. Rafa still gets only R$8,000. What does offer A really cost per month? Guess.
p1.reveal: About 2.9% a month. So the "cheap" 1.9% costs more than offer B's 2.3%.

m1.prompt: Match each part of a loan with what it means.

q1.prompt: A: 1.9% a month, real cost 2.9%. B: 2.3% a month, real cost 2.3%. Which is cheaper?
q1.explanation: Look at the real cost. B is 2.3% and that's all. A is 2.9% with the fee and insurance.

q2.prompt: Why does a lender show a low rate and add fees?
options: People see the low rate first, but the fees make it cost more
q2.explanation: People compare the first number. Extra fees are [[hidden-interest]].
